**Version:** codex-cli 0.163.0, Linux x86_64

Upserting a key inside an inline table with `config/batchWrite` converts the inline table into a standard table, but the comment line above it ends up inside the header brackets. The resulting `config.toml` is invalid and Codex no longer starts.

**Repro.** `config.toml`:
```toml
[features]
# any comment line
multi_agent_v2 = { enabled = true, max_concurrent_threads_per_session = 30 }
```
`config/batchWrite` with `expectedVersion` from `config/read` and edits:
```json
[{"keyPath": "features.multi_agent_v2.max_concurrent_threads_per_session", "value": 21, "mergeStrategy": "upsert"},
 {"keyPath": "features.multi_agent_v2.disable_direct_message", "value": false, "mergeStrategy": "upsert"}]
```
Written result:
```toml
[features]

[# any comment line
features.multi_agent_v2 ]
enabled = true
max_concurrent_threads_per_session = 21
disable_direct_message = false
```
`codex features list` then fails with `Error: failed to load bootstrap configuration … TOML parse error at line 4, column 25`. Without the comment line, the same write produces a valid table.

**Expected:** the file stays valid, either by updating the inline table in place or by keeping the comment above the new table header.

items.title: [Windows] IAB stale-frame retry loop floods browser lifecycle and hangs desktop

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop on Windows can enter a high-volume in-app-browser lifecycle loop after browser-using chats fail or are interrupted. The loop repeatedly calls `executeCdp:DOM.getFrameOwner` for frames that no longer exist, generates tens of thousands of `IAB_LIFECYCLE` records, and coincides with repeated `ChatGPT.exe` hangs.

This appears operationally distinct from the retained-resource and memory-pressure incident tracked in #55151. In this recurrence, memory and system commit were elevated but well below the earlier extreme, and the app-server queue did not saturate.

## Environment

- Windows 10.0.19045
- Package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64`
- Updater/build observed in diagnostics: `26.1013.40934` / `20770`
- Feedback ID: `01a136cf-cc28-7752-bf95-91ab6f040675`

## Observed browser-control loop

Across the affected app-instance logs from `2026-10-19T00:00:25.533Z` through `2026-10-19T01:18:11.903Z`:

- 23,388 `IAB_LIFECYCLE` lines
- 15,720 of those lines reported `Frame with the given id was not found`
- 0 `App server request queue is full` lines
- 0 `App server request expired while queued` lines
- 0 `rendererGone` lines
- 0 `tab is not part of browser session` lines

The peak minute, `00:34Z`, contained 1,893 `IAB_LIFECYCLE` lines, including 1,785 missing-frame errors. The repeated operation was `executeCdp:DOM.getFrameOwner`, accompanied by browser-sidebar owner synchronisation/rebinding.

Traffic was attributed to several concurrent browser-using conversation IDs. The largest source produced 5,152 lifecycle lines and belonged to a LinkedIn/Indeed browser task whose turn eventually failed with a model-capacity error after a long run. Other active browser chats each contributed thousands more. This suggests that failed or interrupted browser work can leave stale frame or ownership work behind, while concurrency amplifies the retry volume.

## Confirmed application hangs

Windows Error Reporting recorded three new `ChatGPT.exe` `AppHangTransient` events:

- 2026-10-19 02:09:56 BST — `1555264b-d31e-43b7-8100-ea917e4de1bc`
- 2026-10-19 02:10:18 BST — `9fac2b22-745f-4449-b582-4afa16e9976f`
- 2026-10-19 02:10:48 BST — `28aaf6e9-971b-48ae-addc-0831524d1cf7`

Immediately before restart, the visible ChatGPT/Codex process group had:

- 72 processes
- 8.454 GiB combined private allocation
- 10.596 GiB working set
- about 7 GiB available physical memory
- about 79.6% system commit

Those values are elevated but materially below the 16.5–17.4 GiB private allocation and 87–89% commit observed in #55151. The complete absence of queue-full and queue-expiry messages in this recurrence is another meaningful difference.

## GPU correlation checked

The user was also doing video work, so GPU contention was investigated. A 24-second NVIDIA sample while the stale-frame loop remained active showed:

- GPU utilisation varied from 3% to 74%, without sustained saturation
- video encoder utilisation remained at 0%
- 2.6–3.6 GiB of 8.2 GiB VRAM was used
- temperature remained 38–39 C

This sample cannot exclude an earlier transient spike, but it does not explain the repeated stale-frame requests or support sustained encoder saturation as the immediate trigger.

## Recovery observation

After Codex restarted, the failed browser-owning chat was archived and the largest active contributors were told to checkpoint, close completed browser tabs through supported controls, verify their inventories, and stop browser work.

A later sample showed 44 processes and 5.658 GiB private allocation. The next five-minute log window contained zero lifecycle, missing-frame, queue, or renderer-gone events.

Restart and cleanup occurred together, so this before/after observation does not isolate causation. It does show that the retry storm was not an unavoidable consequence of the concurrent graphics workload.

## Expected behaviour

- Pending CDP/frame-owner work should be cancelled when a frame navigates, detaches, or is replaced.
- Missing-frame retries should be bounded and use backoff or circuit breaking.
- Browser tabs, ownership bindings, and pending IAB work should be torn down when a chat fails, is interrupted, or reaches `systemError`.
- Background owner synchronisation should not repeatedly rebind an unchanged owner.
- Browser lifecycle work should be isolated per chat so one failed task cannot flood the desktop process.
- Diagnostics should expose browser/tab ownership and stale retained state so users can recover without repeated paid troubleshooting turns.

## Related reports

- #55151 tracks the separate retained-resource and memory/commit-pressure mechanism.
- #54092 and #51296 appear related to stale-frame or CDP failures, but this report includes a repeatable high-volume lifecycle storm, multiple concurrent owners, and Windows `AppHangTransient` correlation.

I can provide the redacted log excerpts and supporting diagnostic artifacts associated with the feedback ID. Credentials, cookies, tokens, and unrelated secrets must remain excluded.

items.title: codex exec: option to skip the global $CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md without changing CODEX_HOME

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI (`codex exec`), 0.162.1

### What feature would you like to see?

A per-run switch that stops Codex from adding the global instructions file (`$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.override.md` or `$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md`) to the prompt, while keeping the normal sign-in in `CODEX_HOME`. For example: `codex exec --ignore-user-instructions`, or a config key that `-c` can set.

Why: tools that call `codex exec` for a narrow, automated job (for example a code reviewer that must follow only the instructions it sends) need a known, recordable prompt. Today every run also receives the user's personal working rules. Those rules can change the output, and the calling tool can't see or record them.

What I checked in `rust-v0.162.1`:
- `app-server/src/message_processor.rs` always constructs `CodexHomeUserInstructionsProvider::new(config.codex_home)`.
- `codex-home/src/instructions/mod.rs` reads `AGENTS.override.md`, then `AGENTS.md`, from that folder.
- `core/src/agents_md.rs` puts these instructions before any project docs. `project_doc_max_bytes` doesn't limit them.
- `--ignore-user-config` skips only `config.toml` (its help says "auth still uses CODEX_HOME"). `--ignore-rules` covers only `.rules` files.

The only workaround is a separate `CODEX_HOME` with its own sign-in, because `CODEX_HOME` holds both the instructions and the login. That works, but users have to sign in twice.

### Additional information

Related: #26806 (letting subagents override inherited personal instructions) and #35706 (showing the complete prompt in `codex debug prompt-input`). It would also help if the `thread.started` event in `codex exec --json` listed the instruction sources that were loaded, as app-server thread responses already do with `instructionSources`.

items.body:
Submitted at the account owner’s explicit request. This report requests a supported diagnosis and recovery procedure, not a bypass of safety controls.

## 请求

我希望在真实安全规则允许的前提下，让Codex长期稳定地只读访问我有权查看的企业微信在线表格，目标origin为`https://doc.weixin.qq.com`。请定位历史URL安全终止的实际评估origin和策略来源，并提供正式复核/恢复流程；不是请求绕过安全检查。

## 环境（本地已核验）

- ChatGPT/Codex macOS桌面应用：26.1013.40934，build20770；Bundle ID `com.openai.codex`。
- macOS27.0.1，build26A434，arm64。
- Clash Verge2.5.8、Mihomo1.19.32为历史诊断记录；已安装系统服务并启用TUN后曾恢复网络。本轮未调整或重新测试其设置。
- 事件时间采用Asia/Shanghai（UTC+8）。

## 两类现象，请分别处理

### A. 网络及浏览器路由

10月18日22:51前多次WebSocket握手超时。启用TUN后的历史测试曾确认目标连接走隧道；22:51:26握手成功，随后原聊天标准浏览器工具读取官方公开帮助页约0.93秒完成，AX及截图成功。

但完整日志显示恢复并不等于长期稳定：22:52仍有4条新的无路由错误，23:11、23:17有pong超时并快速重连；23:45到次日00:01又出现断线、TLS失败和后续握手恢复。未逐次记录TUN状态或睡眠事件，不确定这些后续异常的根因。

### B. URL安全终止

10月18日21:04:35.262和21:50:13.306，原始Computer Use工具返回如下相同文本：

```text
This session has been stopped because Computer Use is not allowed on the current browser URL. Stop your work and send a final message noting why the session has been ended. Note that Computer Use is not allowed on this URL even if the user navigates to it themselves.
```

调用意图与目标业务文档相关，但返回值没有实际评估URL、策略来源、原因类别或复核入口。不能据此确认实际评估的是目标origin，或认定误判。原生Safari路径收到过该终止；未证明内置浏览器目标页面在网络恢复后也会返回同样结果。

21:27:17.946，尝试进入Codex应用自身设置还得到独立错误：

```text
Computer Use is not allowed to use the app 'com.openai.codex' for safety reasons.
```

网络恢复后没有重试目标表格，本轮也没有访问受限页面、换浏览器/会话、直接CDP或脚本获取数据。因此，目标网址当前是否仍会拒绝尚未验证。

## 已检查的权限状态

- 用户提供的设置截图显示：默认浏览Always allow，未列网站例外。
- 本地一般浏览配置只有`approval_mode = "never_ask"`，没有网站级拒绝条目。
- 用户`config.toml`没有相关浏览器/电脑控制配置段。
- 所检查的用户/系统`requirements.toml`以及系统`managed_config.toml`不存在。
- `profiles status -type enrollment`返回DEP: No、MDM enrollment: No；已检查的托管首选项文件不存在，普通应用plist无官方MDM载荷键。
- 这些结果不能排除云端组织策略、会话级保存决定或内置工具安全规则。未取得有效云策略、会话权限决定记录或分类器诊断。
- 本机原始工具输出没有确认`persisted_user_denied`。请勿仅因可见设置允许就把本机归类为保存权限错误。

## 最小脱敏事件摘要

下列均来自原始应用日志或会话工具记录，未复制私有URL或用户数据；应用文件名和会话ID用占位符替代。

| 北京时间 | 记录 |
|---|---|
| 10-18 20:42:38.411 | `[browser-session-registry] reassigned browser use route sourceConversationId=[FORMAL] targetConversationId=[DRAFT]` |
| 20:59:18.783 | `[browser-use-iab-api] No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session [REDACTED]` |
| 21:04:35.262、21:50:13.306 | 原始工具返回上述URL安全终止文本 |
| 22:51:04.074 | `app_server_connection.closed code=1006 failureReason=open_timeout connectionId=159` |
| 22:51:26.279 | `initialize_handshake_result durationMs=811 outcome=success transportKind=websocket` |
| 22:52:02.173—.175 | 4条新的`No ChatGPT browser route is available` |
| 23:11:09.193 → 23:11:11.571 | `failureReason=pong_timeout` → `initialize_handshake_result outcome=success` |
| 23:17:28.205 → 23:17:30.874 | 同上，再次断线并恢复 |
| 23:45:49.228、10-19 00:00:56.218 | `code=1006`；关联错误`Client network socket disconnected before secure TLS connection was established` |
| 10-19 00:01:05.387 | `initialize_handshake_result durationMs=242 outcome=success transportKind=websocket` |

## 相关报告，仅作对照

- [#53154](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53154)：相同URL终止文字及自应用限制；环境和浏览器路径不同，未证明同源。
- [#51942](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51942)：讨论可见允许与保存拒绝冲突；本机尚未验证保存拒绝，错误类型也不同。
- [#52472](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52472)：路由与TUN网络恢复线索相似；本机恢复后仍有路由及网络事件。

上述均为公开用户报告，未将其推测当成官方确认。

## 希望官方回答

1. 两次URL终止的实际评估origin、原因类别、执行组件与策略来源是什么？是否能提供安全的诊断事件编号？
2. 可见网站允许设置之外，是否存在会话保存拒绝或云组织限制？请提供有效策略的正式查询方式。
3. 如果是会话拒绝，是否有保留聊天及其他规则的官方撤销/重新授权流程？
4. 如果是URL分类误判，是否有正式复核渠道；如果是预期限制，该只读在线表格任务是否受支持？
5. 恢复后无路由事件是否为已知问题？请给出确认的修复版本及对已有受影响会话的恢复办法。

如需原始会话编号或更多日志，请指明合适的非公开支持渠道及最小必要字段。不会在公开Issue提供完整分享链接、scode、凭证、企业内容、截图或未经脱敏的会话/日志。

items.title: [Feature] Expose verifiable per-invocation identity to Codex CLI child tools

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: exec
labels.description: Issues related to the `codex exec` subcommand

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
**What variant of Codex are you using?**

Codex CLI, including nested `codex exec` sessions that invoke shell tools.

**What feature would you like to see?**

Please provide a supported, content-free way for a local child tool to verify which Codex invocation launched it. The identity should represent the actual runtime-selected session and, where available, the specific tool/run invocation. It must not be accepted as proof merely because a caller supplied an environment value or argument, and nested Codex sessions must not inherit a parent's identity as if it were their own.

A runtime-issued attestation or another equivalent verifiable interface is fine; this request does not prescribe a particular cryptographic design. The signal should not require exposing prompts, responses, or rollout contents.

**Additional information**

Airo PR #205 needs this to check that a child process was launched by the exact Mission Controller execution that was admitted to dispatch work. `CODEX_THREAD_ID` by itself is not adequate authorization evidence: [#15527](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15527) reports nested `codex exec` commands inheriting the parent thread ID. [#36883](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36883) proposes `AI_AGENT=codex` as an advisory marker, which also does not establish caller identity. The related [#46672](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/46672) asked for a content-free session attestation path or caller-supplied thread ID and was closed as no longer needed; this request adds the requirement that identity be verifiable and not self-asserted.

Useful validation cases would cover a nested invocation receiving its own identity, a parent identity not being reported as the nested caller, and caller-provided environment/argument values not being mistaken for runtime proof.

items.title: Windows desktop — supported pre-receive reservation integration point (source, native ABI, or vendor build)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex desktop app on Windows, x64.

Observed installed package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0`.
Internal Electron package: `openai-codex-electron 26.1013.40934`.
These are static package identifiers, not a claim about the currently loaded process image.

### What feature would you like to see?

A supported **pre-receive reservation integration point** for the Windows desktop client, provided as matching source/build instructions, a native extension ABI, or a vendor build implementing the capability.

#### Use case

We need to integrate a fail-closed Windows synchronization barrier with the first receiver of the existing desktop client, while preserving the current conversation and its in-flight state.

Here, a reservation means actual synchronization ownership acquired **before arming or performing a relevant input read**, and retained while that input is incomplete or being classified. A separately guarded Windows action must remain blocked while a receiver has unresolved or restrictive input. This is an additional application-specific coordination requirement, not a claim that Codex currently promises this behavior.

#### Requested integration

Please identify whether a supported integration is available, and route this request to the desktop/native receiver owner if necessary. We need one of:

- Matching receiver source plus a reproducible, supported build recipe.
- A native extension ABI that acquires a real synchronization reservation before arming/performing the first relevant input read.
- A vendor build implementing that capability.

A post-submit hook, plugin message sender, MessagePort consumer wrapper, or app-server client is insufficient on its own: data can already have been received, queued, or exposed before that callback. A callback could verify previously established ownership, but cannot establish it retroactively.

#### Required contract

- Bind each reservation to receiver identity, instance and generation.
- Propagate actual possession and pending operations across buffers, IPC and callbacks.
- Prevent a stale completion from releasing a newer generation's reservation.
- Retain a blocking state on restriction, uncertainty, incomplete input or loss.
- Define initialization, receiver death, cancellation and handoff behavior, including already-armed reads.
- Specify covered and uncovered paths, including clipboard/IME/files, audio, IPC, network buffering, and scheduled or internal inputs.
- Preserve conversation continuity without assuming that an unchanged conversation ID proves transfer of in-flight synchronization state.

The reservation interface alone would not prove atomicity with an external Windows action; the final native effect boundary would still need separate validation. We are not asking to treat a software ticket followed by a later native call as one atomic operation.

### Additional information

Please provide the supported load point, ABI/version and threading rules, build provenance/licensing or distribution terms, and a way to test ordering using inert witnesses. If this interface does not exist, confirmation and identification of the component required to add it would resolve the acquisition question.

The public CLI/SDK/app-server sources and the documented plugin surfaces are useful integration layers, but we have not established that they expose this first-reader contract in the existing desktop client. We are not requesting a second client as an equivalent replacement without addressing that boundary.

This is a feature/integration request, **not a report of a demonstrated vulnerability in Codex**, and not a request to bypass sandboxing or permissions. No production activation, credential sharing or privileged installation is requested at this stage.

Privacy: no conversation IDs, user paths, credentials, private project history or raw logs are attached. Prepared with Codex assistance and published at the user's explicit request.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
## What issue are you seeing?

My dot-created cloud product-owner threads repeatedly disappear from my visible Codex/ChatGPT desktop navigation. Opening their direct desktop thread links makes them show up again. Earlier, I moved them into a named Section because I could not pin them; they became hard to find again after restarting/resetting my two Macs.

This makes ongoing work difficult to supervise. I have to ask my dot to send the same links again to recover access to the conversations.

## Latest observation

2026-10-19 around 00:42 UTC (October 18 in my local timezone), after I reset/restarted both machines, I reported that all cloud owner threads were missing from my view again.

A read-only control check by my dot at that time returned all six expected cloud owner thread IDs through `cloud_threads.list_threads(children_only=false)`. The dot then resent the original links. No replacement owner threads were created, and no archive/delete operation was performed during this check.

The sidebar symptom is my firsthand report; the assistant did not inspect screenshot pixels or the desktop UI in this diagnostic session. The backend listing confirms the cloud tasks still exist. It does not establish why the UI stopped surfacing them or whether a Section association, filter, cache, sync, or another state is responsible.

## Steps / observed pattern

1. Open cloud task threads created by a dot.
2. Organize them into a named Section for continued access.
3. Later return to the desktop app, including after the reported machine/app restart.
4. The expected cloud threads are no longer visible where I access them.
5. Open the original direct thread links; in prior occurrences this made the threads appear again.

The latest post-restart link-recovery result has not yet been reverified in this diagnostic session. Exact desktop app/build and macOS versions were not captured.

## Expected behavior

Cloud task threads and their user-selected organization should remain discoverable across app/device restarts. Opening a direct link should not be necessary to make an existing task visible again. If a filter or availability limitation explains the view, the UI should make it clear and provide a recovery path.

## Scope

This is separate from the existing-local-thread placement-format read/send failure reported in #52873 and approval-handoff friction in #50521. I am not claiming they share a cause.

Private thread IDs, repository names, project contents, screenshots with unrelated information, and credentials are intentionally omitted. Identifiers can be supplied through private support if needed.

items.title: [Windows] Retained chats/IAB state accumulates 42 renderers, saturates app-server queues, and hangs desktop

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop on Windows became progressively unstable while many chats, recurring jobs, and in-app browser sessions were retained. Chats silently stopped responding, the whole app repeatedly froze or closed, and Windows recorded six `ChatGPT.exe` `AppHangTransient` events within 44 minutes.

The strongest local evidence points to a combined lifecycle/backpressure failure:

1. renderer, app-server, browser, and long-chat state accumulated;
2. the IAB browser entered a very high-volume stale-frame/session lifecycle storm;
3. app-server queues filled or requests expired;
4. severe memory and system-commit pressure amplified the failures;
5. chats became unresponsive and the Electron host hung.

After restarting, closing unused browser tabs, moving 55 chat-bound recurring jobs to 54 fresh chats, and archiving the 54 long source chats, process counts and memory use fell sharply and the app became materially more stable. Those changes occurred together, so the evidence does not isolate one cause or prove a memory leak/garbage-collection defect.

## User impact

- The account moved from 100% to 55% remaining in its seven-day Codex allowance while the user was largely diagnosing and mitigating Codex itself rather than progressing the intended project.
- Several chats appeared to go dead randomly, including the diagnostic chat.
- The user repeatedly had to restart the app.
- The app is now running much better after the mitigation bundle, but the user requests review of usage consumed by failed, interrupted, duplicated, or recovery work.

## Environment

- Windows x64: `Microsoft Windows 10.0.19045`
- Running Microsoft Store package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64`
- App updater: version `26.1013.40934`, build `20770`, production channel, `up_to_date`
- Feedback/session ID for internal correlation: `01a136cf-cc28-7752-bf95-91ab6f040675`

The differing package/updater version strings are reported exactly and not interpreted.

## Confirmed hangs

Windows Error Reporting recorded `ChatGPT.exe` `AppHangTransient` at these local BST times on 18 October 2026:

- 22:29:51
- 22:39:11
- 22:55:43
- 22:56:35
- 23:10:21
- 23:13:42

No useful matching minidump or faulting stack was recovered. Windows reports transient hangs rather than a faulting exception.

## Resource accumulation

An earlier process snapshot measured:

- 42 renderer processes using 8.541 GiB private allocation;
- 19 app-server processes using 3.718 GiB;
- one GPU process using 2.173 GiB;
- 15.541 GiB total visible ChatGPT/Codex private allocation;
- 4,240 MiB available physical memory.

Five later samples measured:

- 16.509–17.401 GiB combined private allocation;
- only 586–1,132 MiB available physical memory;
- 87.33–88.75% system commit.

A separate changing-workload sample counted 52 renderers and 20 app servers. Process roles do not map one-to-one to chats or tabs, and private allocation is not the same as resident physical RAM.

After restart, browser cleanup, and chat migration, a later snapshot measured:

- 10 renderers;
- 2 app servers;
- 4.020 GiB combined private allocation;
- 12,700 MiB available physical memory.

Relative to the earlier 42-renderer snapshot, this is about 76% fewer renderers, 89% fewer app servers, and 74% less private allocation. The workload and app lifetime differ, so this comparison does not isolate causation.

## Browser lifecycle failures

A full scan of the retained 18 October logs found:

- 59,476 `IAB_LIFECYCLE` entries;
- 36,226 `Frame with the given id was not found` failures;
- 38 `tab is not part of browser session` failures.

Across 70 active minutes from 21:05–22:15 UTC, `IAB_LIFECYCLE` traffic had a median of 534 entries per active minute, a mean of 638.4, and a maximum of 2,112 in one minute.

At `21:29:52.058Z`, 0.672 seconds after the first Windows-recorded hang time, the log reported that a tab was not part of its browser session.

## App-server queue saturation

The retained day logs contain:

- 1,878 `App server request queue is full` messages, spanning `21:09:46–23:01:52Z`;
- 1,176 `App server request expired while queued` messages, spanning `21:01:10–23:53:55Z`.

Logs show filesystem, attachment, thread-list, tail-history, configuration, hook, model, MCP, and other work competing through app-server request handling. Queue failure directly explains why individual chats and controls can stop responding even when the main process remains open.

## Correlation around each hang

Counts below cover plus or minus 120 seconds around each WER event. The 21:55 and 21:56 windows overlap, so those totals are not independent.

| Hang UTC | IAB lifecycle | Missing frame | Tab/session mismatch | Queue expired | Filesystem missing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 21:29:51 | 2,369 | 1,767 | 3 | 0 | 96 |
| 21:39:11 | 790 | 328 | 0 | 70 | 0 |
| 21:55:43 | 3,509 | 2,326 | 0 | 0 | 89 |
| 21:56:35 | 2,839 | 1,644 | 0 | 0 | 91 |
| 22:10:21 | 5,008 | 3,345 | 2 | 33 | 13 |
| 22:13:42 | 3,290 | 2,387 | 1 | 58 | 0 |

Every confirmed hang is surrounded by hundreds or thousands of browser lifecycle and missing-frame entries.

## Concurrent long-chat workload

- The user observed failures while several chats were working and saw many long histories and retained browser tabs.
- Before migration, one recent-page snapshot reported 25 active chats.
- After restart/migration, a later recent-page snapshot reported 2 active and 48 idle.
- Fifty-five chat-bound recurring jobs were moved to 54 fresh chats and all 54 old owners were archived.
- Stability subsequently improved by the user's observation.

The desktop app exposes no supported mapping from renderer/app-server processes or retained browser tabs to their owning chats, preventing direct attribution.

## Negative evidence and limits

- No retained 18 October log line matched `rendererGone`, an explicit out-of-memory event, or a GPU-crash category.
- No useful 18 October minidump or native faulting stack was recovered.
- Absence of an explicit OOM log does not negate independently measured memory/commit pressure.
- A controlled one-variable reproduction was not attempted because deliberately recreating the instability risked active work.
- The stale-frame storm may be a cause, amplifier, or symptom. The temporal association is strong, but the internal defect is not proven.

## Expected behavior

- Completed browser tabs, idle renderers, app-server resources, and long-chat history state should be reclaimed automatically.
- Background hydration, browser lifecycle work, and scheduled chats should not starve interactive requests.
- Interactive messages and recovery controls should receive priority over bulk/background work.
- The app should show which chat or browser owns resource use and warn before retained state reaches a destabilising level.
- A compact/checkpoint-and-continue recovery path should preserve work without forcing repeated paid diagnostic turns.
- One stale browser frame, oversized history, or slow chat should fail in isolation rather than hanging the app.

## Related issues

- #54092 — stale-frame errors and CDP timeouts
- #51296 and #55132 — Windows main-process crashes around IAB teardown
- #37401 — local app-server queue saturation blocking messages
- #36189 — long-thread hydration/backpressure starving app-server requests

This report appears related to all four mechanisms but has a distinct combined trigger and measured resource footprint.

## Diagnostic availability and privacy

The local package retains the exact six WER report IDs, per-hang counts, process snapshots, full ranked analysis, charts, and redacted submission receipts. The user authorises sharing relevant chat content, identifiers, titles, filesystem paths, diagnostic logs, and project context for this investigation. Credentials, access tokens, cookies, authentication material, and unrelated secrets must remain excluded. Raw logs should be reviewed/redacted before any upload.

This diagnosis was produced with AI-assisted log and process analysis. All causal limits above are intentional.

items.body:
Uso ChatGPT Work con acceso local en Windows. La revisión automática bloqueó la creación de un ZIP alegando telemetría HTTPS hacia un destino externo no autorizado. Un rechazo anterior mencionó dc.services.visualstudio.com.

El script revisado solo copia archivos locales, calcula hashes SHA-256 y comprime. No invoca compilaciones ni contiene llamadas de red.

Comando:
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "work\Build-JournalPackage.ps1"

Mensaje exacto:
“Aunque el empaquetado local está autorizado, esta ejecución vuelve a generar una conexión de telemetría HTTPS a un destino externo no aprobado, cuya divulgación de metadatos no fue autorizada”.

Entorno:
- Windows, ChatGPT Work con acceso local.
- Windows PowerShell.
- Sandbox: workspace-write.
- Aprobación granular con revisión automática.
- Red restringida por lista de dominios autorizados.

El rechazo no proporciona PID ni ejecutable emisor. En el entorno accesible, CODEX_HOME no está definido y no encontramos las carpetas .codex/sessions, .codex/archived_sessions ni .codex/.sandbox/sandbox.log.

Escribir / en el compositor tampoco mostró una opción de feedback.

Solicito:
1. Cómo identificar el proceso que intenta conectarse, sin repetir la operación bloqueada.
2. Dónde obtener los registros correspondientes a esta modalidad de Work.
3. Cómo continuar el empaquetado local sin autorizar telemetría ni ampliar permisos.

La instalación funcional del proyecto permanece intacta. No adjunto código privado, respaldos ni credenciales.

items.title: Prune unused standalone releases after successful installation
items.body:
Prune unused standalone releases after successful installation

## What changed

Clean up older standalone releases after verifying the installed command, while holding the install lock. Retain the current and previously selected releases, along with releases used by running Codex processes or bundled helpers.

Record selection history for all standalone installs and preserve it on no-op installs. Only remove validated, installer-owned release directories; skip cleanup when filesystem or process inspection cannot establish that removal is safe. Recheck process usage after moving a release aside and restore it if it is in use.

## Testing

Add installer regression coverage for running helpers, helpers started during cleanup, repeated installs, failed installs, downgrades, and preservation of unowned directories and symlinks.

items.title: Admin console: edit a workspace MCP plugin's description, icon and OAuth client secret in place

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

The workspace plugin catalog in the ChatGPT admin console (admin.openai.com, Plugins), on ChatGPT Business. The plugin is a remote MCP server made with **Create MCP plugin**, signing in through OAuth with a pre-registered Microsoft Entra ID client (`client_secret_post`).

### What feature would you like to see?

Let a workspace admin change an existing workspace plugin in place, without uploading a new package or making the plugin again:

1. its description;
2. its icon;
3. its authentication settings: above all a new OAuth client secret, but also the client ID, scopes and token endpoint auth method entered at Create, and a re-read of the server's OAuth metadata after it changes.

Today the plugin's page in the admin console has no edit control for any of these. **Plugin actions** offers only **Download plugin** and **Upload new version**, and Upload new version takes the whole plugin as an archive (`.tar.gz`, `.tgz` or `.zip`). [Package your plugin](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins) says to "keep the client secret out of the package", so it isn't clear whether an upload keeps the secret entered at Create. The tool list does update in place (**Tools**, **Refresh**), as do the permission and installation settings.

### Additional information

What this has cost one workspace in the last two weeks:

- **Description.** Our mail plugin's card still says it never sends mail. The server now also sends internal mail, after the person approves a preview. The tool list refreshed in place, but correcting the card means replacing the live plugin's whole package, so we left the card out of date rather than risk everyone's sign-in.
- **Icon.** It can only be set at Create. A plugin made without one has to be deleted and made again, with a new client secret, and then every person connects again.
- **Client secret.** Entra ID client secrets expire; one of ours lasts six months. An existing plugin has no field for a new secret, so each rotation means rebuilding the plugin, and if the secret lapses first, every person's sign-in renewals stop at once. A secret pasted wrongly at Create (its ID instead of its value) could likewise only be fixed by making the plugin again.
- **Authentication settings.** After the server's sign-in metadata changed (scopes, issuer), ChatGPT kept the old settings. The fix was to rebuild the plugin and have each person reconnect, which left our staff without it in the meantime. Making the replacement also failed with `409 plugins_conflict` until its name differed from the admin's own personal plugin.

An edit form on the plugin's page, or an admin API for these settings, would remove the need for all four.

Related: #39508 (a deleted workspace plugin keeps its name, which breaks delete-and-recreate) and #36929 (updating a shared workspace plugin from Codex Desktop).

No tokens, workspace or tenant identifiers, client IDs, plugin contents, hostnames or customer data are included.

items.title: Android Remote and Windows desktop expose old imported history differently; investigate recency vs metadata-update ordering

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### Summary

On Android Codex Remote connected to a Windows desktop host, the user can discover and open old local conversations, including imported Claude Code sessions, that are not prominent in the desktop history. The user initially perceived them as unfamiliar conversations.

This report concerns cross-client history discoverability/ordering and imported-session presentation. Accessing existing host history is expected; this report does **not** claim that showing an old conversation alone is a bug, that other users' history is exposed, or that data was deleted.

### Environment

- Windows desktop package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64` (read from the running ChatGPT executable path)
- Active local backend: `codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`
- Remote client: ChatGPT on Android, exact app/Android versions not collected
- Desktop sidebar persisted preferences: project grouping, chat sorting `updated_at`
- Observed on October 18–19, 2026 (UTC+08:00)

### Observed behavior and read-only evidence

The user supplied seven mobile screenshots covering six distinct host threads. Every sampled thread could be matched to local history. Two imported-session examples are anonymized below:

- **A:** imported from a local Claude Code session on October 7, 2026. Its preview/title is a raw `<task-notification>` block rather than an intelligible human request.
- **B:** imported from a local Claude Code worktree session on August 11, 2026.

Import success records in an October 9 backup map the original local Claude files to these exact Codex threads. Both are currently unarchived, with `source=vscode`, `originator=Codex Desktop`, `thread_source=null`, and no project assignment.

Local backend logs explicitly show Android client `codex_chatgpt_android_remote` issuing `thread/resume` for A at 2026-10-18 23:38:35 +08:00 and B at 23:39:32 +08:00. The logs show `apply_rollout_reconstruction` of existing history, not a new Claude import.

At read-only inspection:

- A: `updated_at=2026-10-18 23:38:35 +08:00`, `recency_at=2026-08-07 06:52:16 +08:00`.
- B: `updated_at=2026-10-18 23:39:32 +08:00`, `recency_at=2026-08-05 21:28:37 +08:00`.

Among unarchived rows with interactive source values, descending `updated_at` places A/B at approximately positions 10/7, while descending `recency_at` places them at 83/88. These are diagnostic SQL rankings, **not captured client result positions**. They demonstrate how different timestamp selection can make the same history prominent or obscure.

A separate old desktop document conversation renders a literal `:codex-file-citation{path="..." purpose="output"}` string on Android instead of a usable file reference. Imported sessions also preserve raw external tool-call/result text.

### Expected behavior

- History ordering/discovery should be understandable and consistent across desktop and Android, or differences should be made explicit.
- If one surface uses last conversational activity and another uses metadata/resume update time, merely viewing old history should not unexpectedly make it look like recent work on only one surface.
- Imported session rows should provide an intelligible title/source indication. Background notifications should not become the apparent human-authored request.
- File-reference directives should render appropriately or provide a clear fallback.

### Reproduction / investigation recipe

This is an observed-state report; a fresh-install controlled reproduction has **not** been performed.

1. Have a Windows host with old imported Claude sessions and ordinary old desktop/extension threads.
2. Keep desktop sidebar in project grouping with enough history to paginate.
3. Connect Android Remote to the same host and compare discoverable conversations.
4. Open an old imported thread on Android without sending a new message.
5. Compare desktop/Android listing positions and requested `thread/list` filters, pagination and sort key; compare `updatedAt` versus `recencyAt`.
6. Check whether raw notification previews and file-reference directives are shown.

### Limitations / confounders

- Exact Android versus desktop `thread/list` request bodies were not captured. A timestamp/filter mismatch is a **candidate explanation**, not a confirmed implementation root cause.
- The user's history was backed up/restored during a local reinstall on October 9. The restoration script cleared the external import registry while retaining conversation history. Original import success records survive in the earlier backup. This may affect provenance presentation and should be considered when reproducing.
- Reading/resuming a thread can update metadata; the inspection should not be interpreted as a controlled before/after experiment.
- No settings, conversation data, archive state, or indexes were changed during this investigation. No restart/reset/reimport was attempted.

### Related reports checked

- #47150 — recent project conversation drops down desktop history after iOS Remote activity; different platform and active-message case.
- #48423 — imported agent notifications misattributed as user messages and raw tool logs; closely related to the confusing imported preview, but does not cover this cross-client listing observation.

Prepared with Codex assistance. Usernames, device names, local paths, thread IDs, original conversation contents, screenshots, credentials and full logs have been omitted from this public report. Maintainers can request a focused, sanitized reproduction or diagnostic follow-up.

items.title: Add observation-only model request lifecycle hooks
items.body:
Add observation-only model request lifecycle hooks

## What changed

- Add `PreModelRequest` and `PostModelRequest` hooks around model request attempts, including retries. Pass model, session, turn, and optional subagent context; report completion, failure, or cancellation with errors and token usage when available.
- Treat hook output as diagnostic data without allowing it to veto requests or alter model context. Wait for synchronous post-request hooks before dispatching tools, while asynchronous hooks allow streaming tool dispatch to continue.
- Apply memory-consolidation hook filtering and expose the new events through configuration, protocol schemas, generated clients, and the hooks browser.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for failures and retries, ignored control directives, cancellation, synchronous and asynchronous tool ordering, interrupted-turn resume and token accounting, and memory-consolidation filtering. Update hook schema fixtures and hooks browser snapshots.

items.body:
### App version and platform

- ChatGPT/Codex macOS desktop app **26.1013.40934**, build **20770**, production channel (installed application metadata).
- **macOS 26.7.1**, build **25G241**.
- Observed **October 18, 2026**.
- The configured updater reports **up_to_date**.
- Subscription/account identifiers are omitted from this public report.

### Problem

After restarting the desktop app, the user observed two problems in the same account and workspace:

1. The composer shows **Ask for approval**, but the entire permission selector is grayed out and cannot be opened to select **Approve for me**. User screenshots show the disabled control while the chat is idle. The user reports encountering this with new sessions.
2. The user's existing dot, named **Cosmo**, disappeared from the sidebar. Switching the sidebar between Codex and ChatGPT did not reveal it.

The user confirmed that they did not change accounts, workspaces, or approval settings. **View → Reload Window did not resolve the disabled selector**, according to the user's follow-up.

### Expected behavior

- The approval selector remains usable where the selected execution environment permits it.
- The saved **Approve for me** preference is honored, or the app explains any actual policy restriction.
- An existing dot remains discoverable after restarting.
- A configuration-loading failure should have an actionable recovery/error state rather than leaving controls silently disabled or a dot absent.

### Observed diagnostic evidence

Read-only inspection of the saved app preferences found **guardian-approvals** selected for both the local and durable hosts, including the preferred non-full-access mode. The saved visibility entry has guardian approvals enabled.

The current local chat's turn-start diagnostics instead show:
- approvals reviewer: **user**
- permission profile: **:workspace**
- a granular approval policy with sandbox/rules/skill approvals false and request_permissions/mcp_elicitations true.

No explicit approval-policy override or `features.guardian_approval = false` was found in the user configuration inspected. No requirements file was found at the standard local paths checked. This does not establish the absence of account-side or other managed restrictions.

Startup logs contain these sanitized errors:

```text
2026-10-18T21:26:01.263Z
Statsig: error while bootstrapping post-login client
attemptNumber=6
errorMessage="Timed out while fetching post-login Statsig bootstrap"
rendererWindowAppearance=primary

2026-10-18T21:27:12.882Z
Statsig: error while bootstrapping post-login client
attemptNumber=6
errorMessage="Timed out while fetching post-login Statsig bootstrap"
rendererWindowAppearance=avatarOverlay
```

The saved sidebar cache still contains Cosmo's profile and main-thread association. That cached profile is marked active but was last updated **October 7**; it is **not proof of the dot's current server-side state**. Opening the cached main-thread ID through the app navigation tool returned navigation success, but restoration of the dot UI/sidebar was not verified.

### Reproduction sequence reported/observed

1. Start with an existing named dot and saved Approve for me preference.
2. Restart the desktop app without changing account or workspace.
3. Observe the dot missing from the sidebar.
4. Open a local chat and observe the Ask for approval selector disabled.
5. Switch the sidebar between Codex and ChatGPT: dot remains absent.
6. Reload Window: user reports the approval selector remains disabled.

This is an observed sequence, not a deterministic minimal reproduction.

### Investigation request

Please investigate whether failed account feature initialization can leave the permission-selector configuration pending/unavailable and hide an existing dot, and whether subsequent initialization/reload properly restores these surfaces. The temporal association and logs are an investigation lead; **a shared root cause has not been established**. No authenticated bootstrap network capture or response-body timing was collected.

Possibly related: #52010 (macOS dot unavailable after Statsig timeouts), #54600 (feature availability affected by bootstrap timeouts), and #49622 (macOS bootstrap timeout/fallback behavior). This report additionally documents the disabled approval selector despite a saved automatic-review preference.

Only this sanitized text is submitted. No screenshots, raw logs, account IDs, private thread IDs, transcripts, credentials, or unrelated project information are attached. No app binaries or permission configuration were modified, and no other running chats were stopped.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

items.body:
## Environment
ChatGPT/Codex desktop **26.1013.31256 (build 20586)**, Apple M4 MacBook Air, 16 GB RAM, macOS 26.5.1. Observed October 18, 2026. Local execution with multiple plugins and scheduled tasks enabled.

## Observed behavior
After a full desktop restart around 20:56 UTC, repeated copies of local tool services accumulated while investigating memory usage. This was active diagnostic use, not a controlled idle test. Existing chats and background/scheduled activity may contribute.

| Measurement | Approximately 21:07 UTC | 21:34:53 UTC |
|---|---:|---:|
| App and descendant processes, summed memory footprint | 6035 MiB | 9732 MiB |
| App-family process count | 111 | 198 |
| Node helper processes | 78 | 156 |
| Node helper summed footprint | 2273 MiB | 4543 MiB |
| System swap used | 2656 MiB | 5095 MiB |
| Memory pressure | Yellow | Yellow |

Measurements used process ancestry and macOS `top` memory values. These are summed process footprints, **not unique physical RAM**, and other apps were running.

Earlier, 11 concurrent copies each of code-review, app-tools, Todoist and several other local helper services were observed. The 11 code-review processes totaled approximately 942 MiB. This does not mean 11 reviews were actively running.

The desktop log recorded **29 code-review server startup events across 27 distinct thread IDs** between launch and approximately 21:35 UTC. Some new IDs also had these messages:

```text
Received turn/started for unknown conversation
Conversation state not found
Received turn/completed for unknown conversation
```

Their origin and connection to retained processes remain unresolved.

Archiving one idle chat resulted in that chat reporting `notLoaded`, but overall process counts continued to grow. There is no immediate before/after sample or PID-to-thread mapping proving which processes that archive released. No plugins were disabled and no helper processes were manually killed.

## Expected behavior / requested investigation
Please investigate lifecycle and cleanup of per-thread MCP/tool servers, including internal or transient threads, restored chats and scheduled activity. Determine whether servers remain alive after their owning work completes or unloads, and whether bounded retention or shared services can avoid the memory amplification without disabling functionality.

This is a **suspected session/tool-process retention bug, not a proven heap leak**. A minimal reproduction and exact trigger are not yet established. Local inspection suggests a three-hour renderer inactivity retention policy and a ten-eligible-thread cap; please confirm how these interact with internal threads and server cleanup.

## Privacy
This report intentionally excludes chat contents, chat titles, thread identifiers, account details and raw logs. Sanitized measurements and relevant log excerpts can be supplied separately if needed.

items.body:
### App version and platform

ChatGPT desktop, powered by Codex & OWL: **26.1013.40934, build 20770**, on an Apple Silicon Mac with **8 GB RAM**.

### Problem and impact

**The newest desktop app pushes the Mac into yellow memory pressure and interferes with the user's work during ordinary chat use and lightweight diagnostics.** No local build or large test run was in progress during the measurements. Closing only the app restored normal memory pressure; reopening it recreated substantial memory use. Restarting the app did not provide a lasting practical resolution.

### Memory measurements

Five samples on October 18, 2026, 30 seconds apart over two minutes:

| Sample | App and process-family footprint (MiB) | Largest renderer footprint (MiB) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3,681.3 | 763.4 |
| 2 | 3,735.0 | 794.8 |
| 3 | 3,658.5 | 763.8 |
| 4 | 3,688.6 | 769.6 |
| 5 | 3,689.2 | 773.4 |

Measured with macOS `proc_pid_rusage` physical footprints, counting each PID once and including backend/tool helpers plus a small diagnostic probe. Summed footprints are an accounting approximation, not unique physical RAM.

The app family held approximately **3.57–3.65 GiB** during that window; later samples approached **3.8 GiB**. Activity Monitor shortly after an app relaunch showed a new renderer at **976.5 MB**, **6.74 GB total memory used**, **3.16 GB compressed**, zero swap, and yellow pressure.

These measurements establish high memory use and work disruption. They do not prove an indefinitely monotonic leak or identify the retaining allocation.

### Rollback is not a usable workaround

Reverting to **26.715.21425 (build 5488)** resolved the memory problem according to the user, but the old app could not resume saved conversations:

```text
Failed to resume chat
paginated threads do not support initialTurnsPage; use turnsBackwardsCursor and itemsBackwardsCursor
```

An affected conversation remained readable through the current API. The lower-memory rollback result is user-observed, not a matched instrumented workload comparison, because the old build cannot load the same chat.

### Requested resolution

Please investigate current-build memory use and provide a supported fix or mitigation that keeps existing conversations usable. The user needs the app to function on an 8 GB Mac without overwhelming the machine or requiring loss of conversation access.

No raw logs, private chat contents or IDs, account identifiers, local paths, or unrelated operational/environment details are included. Submitted by Codex at the user's explicit request.

https://chatgpt.com/plugins?category=creativity

the UI displays:

```text
Nie udało się załadować wtyczek
cloudflare_challenge
```

English: "Failed to load plugins — cloudflare_challenge."

The category contains no usable plugin results, so browsing/searching for Figma through this view is blocked. Clicking **Ponów / Retry** reproduces the same error.

The built-in **Help → Report a bug** flow also fails. A report can be composed, but submitting it repeatedly displays:

```text
Nie udało się przesłać opinii. Spróbuj ponownie
```

English: "Failed to submit feedback. Try again."

No successful feedback confirmation or feedback ID was received. This makes the normal reporting path unavailable during the plugin-directory failure.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed repeatedly on the affected installation; the initial trigger for the challenge has not been isolated:

1. While signed in, open the plugin directory in the desktop app's in-app browser.
2. Select the Creativity category, or open the URL above.
3. Observe the empty directory and `cloudflare_challenge` error.
4. Click Retry; the same error remains.
5. Open the profile menu → Help → Report a bug.
6. Select Bug, enter a description, and submit.
7. Observe "Failed to submit feedback. Try again." Repeating submission does not produce confirmation.

### What is the expected behavior?

The supported first-party in-app browser should load the plugin directory and allow searching/browsing. If verification is needed, provide an actionable recovery path.

The feedback form should successfully submit a bug report, or provide a usable alternative when its submission fails.

### Additional information

The affected user also reports that Figma authorization succeeds far enough to return from Figma to ChatGPT, where **"OAuth state not found"** appears. A subsequent message says the plugin connection could not be loaded. Figma remains uninstalled according to the plugin status. Context7 installed successfully and its documentation tools work in the same conversation.

The directory and feedback failures were observed directly through the UI. The Figma OAuth error is user-reported. The feedback endpoint's network response was not captured, so a shared root cause between these symptoms is not asserted.

Potentially related reports:

- #54924: another plugin installation fails with "OAuth state not found".
- #53384: Windows desktop Cloudflare failures with an unavailable feedback submission path, but different primary UI symptoms.

This report contains only reproduction steps and displayed errors; no account identifiers, authentication data, private project details, raw logs, or unredacted screenshots are attached.

labels.name: bug

labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Summary

I am a ChatGPT **Pro** subscriber using the unified **Windows desktop app**, specifically the **ChatGPT** side (the main selector presents **ChatGPT** and **Codex**). Since approximately early October 2026 and the recent desktop/product updates, project and conversation management has become unreliable across **multiple** projects and chats.

**I have not used Dots.** This is not a dot-created conversation workflow.

These capabilities previously worked for me. I am not asserting that Dots or a specific model release caused the regression; the timing is observational.

## Observed problems

### 1. Projects disappear from the desktop UI / search

- I create a new project through the desktop **ChatGPT** interface, selecting a local GitHub folder for permitted file access.
- The new project does **not appear in desktop project navigation or project search**.
- After I fully quit and restart the desktop app, the project **may reappear**.
- That project does **not appear on ChatGPT.com** under my account.
- Similar visibility/organization failures affect other projects, not only this new example.

I understand that local-folder projects and cloud ChatGPT Projects may have different intended sync semantics. Regardless, a created project should not be invisible in the same desktop app until a restart, and the UI should clearly distinguish local-only from cloud-synced projects.

### 2. Conversations disappear from the left sidebar but remain available via Search

- **Multiple** chats/threads have repeatedly disappeared from the left sidebar and expected project navigation.
- Searching finds some of these same missing conversations, which can still be opened.
- This happens repeatedly across different conversations and projects, not just one older chat falling out of the short recent-history list.
- The sidebar/project lists do not reliably reflect content accessible through Search.

### 3. Existing conversations cannot reliably be moved into projects

- **Move to project** does not offer the expected project in some cases, or the move does not work.
- Dragging a conversation into the project also fails.
- I cannot reliably organize related conversations into their intended project.

### 4. Previously available local-folder selection for new ChatGPT conversations is no longer available

- Previously I could create a ChatGPT desktop workflow with access to a local repository folder.
- Now, when starting a **new ChatGPT** conversation, I cannot find or use that folder-selection option.
- The current top-level desktop selector is **ChatGPT / Codex**; instructions referring to a separate top-level **Work** selector do not match the interface I see.
- I would like confirmation whether the prior folder-attachment flow was relocated, intentionally changed, entitlement-gated, or broken for this installation.

### 5. Desktop/web navigation and project state are inconsistent

- With the same ChatGPT account, the desktop and web do not expose the same projects and conversation organization.
- I cannot tell from the UI which project/chat changes were saved durably and which remain local-only.
- This breaks a long-running development workflow that depends on persistent conversations and authorized access to local GitHub repositories.

## Environment

- Platform: Windows, unified ChatGPT/Codex desktop application, **ChatGPT surface**
- Account: ChatGPT Pro
- Onset: approximately early October 2026, following recent updates
- Date of report: 2026-10-18
- Exact current build: not independently collected for this report; can supply privately or in a follow-up
- Dots used: **No**
- Scope: **multiple existing projects and conversations**, not an isolated new project

## Minimal reproduction sequences

**A — Project visibility**
1. In the Windows desktop ChatGPT side, create a project associated with a local folder.
2. Try to find it in project navigation and project search immediately.
3. Fully quit/relaunch the desktop app; check again (project may now appear).
4. Compare with ChatGPT.com signed into the same account. Please clarify whether a locally associated project is intentionally desktop-only, and display that status clearly.

**B — Missing sidebar history**
1. Open the Windows desktop app with existing chats/projects.
2. Notice some previous conversations are absent from left navigation.
3. Search for a known missing chat; it is still found and can be opened.
4. Return to normal navigation; the conversation/project does not reliably become visible.

**C — Move failure**
1. Open an existing conversation.
2. Try **Move to project** or dragging onto the intended sidebar project.
3. The project may be absent from the destination list or the operation fails.

**D — Local folder access**
1. Start a new ChatGPT conversation in the current unified desktop interface.
2. Attempt to select a local repository folder as previously supported.
3. The previous control/flow is unavailable.

## Expected behavior

- Newly created projects should remain discoverable immediately, regardless of whether they are local-only or cloud projects.
- Local versus cloud project/sync status should be explicit.
- Sidebar, project membership, Search, and saved thread state should agree.
- Supported move operations should persist or return a clear actionable error.
- Authorized local-folder access should have a discoverable, documented workflow, or an explicit deprecation explanation.
- Updates should not make existing work appear lost.

## Impact and request

This is a **high-impact regression** for a Pro user managing multiple substantial coding and documentation projects. Rebuilding projects or resetting local state could risk existing history.

Please investigate the desktop project catalog/sidebar hydration, project membership persistence, and local-folder selection UX. I would appreciate a **non-destructive recovery path** and clarification of the supported cloud-project + local-folder workflow.

I have deliberately **not posted private project names, repository paths, chat IDs, tokens, logs, or screenshots** in this public issue. I can provide redacted reproduction evidence and the exact desktop build when requested.

## Related reports (similar symptoms; root cause not assumed)

- #19290 — chats missing from sidebar but accessible via search
- #55014 — local projects missing after update
- #53761 — desktop project moves do not persist
- #51381 — regression in Move to project availability
- #49047 — project/local Work session association problems
- #34300 — local-folder projects and ordinary Chat organization limitations

These may overlap, but this report captures the concurrent symptoms experienced within the ChatGPT side of the Windows desktop app, without Dots usage.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Codex turned a proposal-editing and wiki migration task into an unrequested document-converter/toolchain setup. The intended workflow was for the LLM to load Markdown into its context and directly generate TeX.

The user had established that collaborators would author wiki Markdown and Codex would serve as proofreader, typesetter, bibliographer, and diagrammer. When asked to copy the existing TeX proposal and create its organized wiki equivalent, the agent chose Pandoc without establishing that a converter matched the intended workflow.

Observed actions included downloading Pandoc and Tectonic into a temporary directory, creating a temporary Python virtual environment, downloading micromamba while pursuing PDF tooling, and running three Pandoc conversion previews. Proposal files were copied and PDFs built, but no wiki pages had been written when the user interrupted.

The user stopped the task over the Pandoc choice and subsequently clarified: the LLM should load the Markdown into context and generate TeX directly. The interruption was honored. The unwanted toolchain detour left the requested wiki work unfinished and required the user to correct the approach.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is a single observed session, not a confirmed deterministic reproduction. Repository names and proposal content are omitted.

1. Establish a workflow with a private working repository, a shared proposal repository, and a shared Markdown wiki. Explain that collaborators edit the wiki and Codex handles editorial work and TeX production.
2. Ask Codex to copy the existing proposal TeX to the shared repository and generate the equivalent wiki Markdown, organized into sections and subsections, separating proposal content from supporting information.
3. Observe Codex choosing Pandoc and bootstrapping additional tools before producing wiki pages.
4. Interrupt the task and clarify that the intended conversion is direct LLM reading and writing from context.

### What is the expected behavior?

The LLM reads the existing content into context and directly writes the corresponding Markdown or TeX, preserving meaning, citations, figures, tables, and section structure. Ongoing production reads the current wiki Markdown into context and directly generates TeX. The agent should keep its implementation aligned with this editorial workflow and avoid introducing an unnecessary conversion pipeline.

### Additional information

- Category: agent behavior, task interpretation, and unnecessary workflow expansion.
- Platform: macOS, Apple Silicon. The locally installed CLI reports `codex-cli 0.163.0`; the active app/runtime build was not independently identified.
- The explicit objection to Pandoc was provided when the user interrupted; it was not an earlier explicit prohibition that the agent ignored.
- No wiki pages were written, and no proposal changes were committed or pushed.
- The agent subsequently recorded direct LLM authoring and the no-Pandoc constraint in the local repository guidance.
- Submitted by Codex at the user's explicit request. Private repository identifiers, proposal text, and session logs are excluded.

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?
Codex Desktop App on Windows, with a ChatGPT Plus subscription.

### What feature would you like to see?
Please provide an optional **weekly-quota-first mode** for Codex Desktop, where the user can continue working while their weekly allowance remains instead of being blocked by an exhausted 5-hour usage window.

An alternative would be to let users choose between the current 5-hour windows and a flexible weekly allowance.

### Why is this needed?
I use Codex Desktop for several ongoing workflows, including:
- A career-search agent that researches job listings and monitors application responses;
- CRM / Bitrix24 architecture and business-process analysis;
- Several separate freelance research agents and project evaluations.

These are multi-step workflows that require a continuous working session. In one recent session, my 5-hour allowance reached **0%** while the weekly allowance still showed **65% remaining**. The app required waiting for the short-term reset before continuing.

The problem is not necessarily the total weekly allocation. It is that the additional 5-hour limit interrupts legitimate project work and makes it difficult to plan multi-agent sessions. A user may still have substantial weekly usage available yet be unable to complete a workflow at that moment.

### Proposed behavior
1. Offer an opt-in mode that draws from the existing weekly quota without a separate 5-hour hard stop, subject to reasonable safeguards.
2. If such a mode is not feasible, allow unused weekly allowance to provide a limited continuation budget after the 5-hour limit is exhausted.
3. Clearly display remaining allowance and reset timing in the desktop UI.
4. For long-running tasks, provide checkpoint/resume support so interruption does not require manually reconstructing a workflow.

This is **not a request for unlimited usage**. It is a request for more predictable scheduling and flexibility with the allowance already provided.

### Related discussion
- #40524 — Let Plus Users Choose How to Consume Their Weekly Codex Quota
- #41004 — Make the 5-hour and weekly Codex quotas sequential instead of concurrent

Thank you for considering this usability improvement.

### What issue are you seeing?

continuing to scroll after reaching the top or bottom of the transcript can insert raw mouse-report fragments into the composer:

`[<64;125;28M[<64;125;28M`

This also interrupts the running agent, without me pressing Escape.

This appears to be a recurrence of https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49184, which was closed as fixed in 0.159.0.

An isolated pseudo-terminal test reproduced the exact text using the crossterm revision pinned by both 0.163.0 and current main (8c076942cb). Sending two `ESC[<64;125;28M` reports, each split after the leading Escape byte with a 1 ms gap, produces two Escape key events followed by the literal report tails. Sending each report intact produces normal wheel-up events. This demonstrates a parser failure consistent with the symptoms; the actual bytes from the affected Ghostty session have not been captured.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Launch Codex CLI 0.163.0 in Ghostty using the default fullscreen interface.
2. Open a conversation long enough to scroll through.
3. Start an agent turn and, while it is running, scroll to the top or bottom of the transcript.
4. Continue scrolling in the same direction after reaching the boundary.
5. Observe that mouse-report fragments can appear in the composer and the active turn is interrupted.

### What is the expected behavior?

Scrolling should neither insert text into the composer nor interrupt an active turn.

### Additional information

The issue appears to be as follows. Crossterm’s Unix input reader can mistake a partial mouse-report sequence for a standalone Escape key. If a read ends just after the leading Escape byte, it emits Escape immediately and interprets the remaining bytes as ordinary text.

In Codex, this can interrupt the running agent and insert fragments like [<64;125;28M into the composer. The reader should briefly wait for a possible continuation before treating Escape as a keypress.

items.title: [Windows] Five main-process crashes immediately after IAB tab close; also occurs unlocked

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

App-reported version: 26.1013.40934; build: 20770; release channel: prod.
Installed Windows package: OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64.
The built-in update check returned `up_to_date` on 2026-10-19.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, version 10.0.26300, build 26300, x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

The entire Codex desktop window disappears and the user must manually relaunch the application. This is not only an interrupted agent turn.

**Update: a further crash occurred while the computer was unlocked and the Codex window was focused. Screen lock and Modern Standby are not necessary conditions. The initial lock/sleep association must not be treated as an established cause.**

Read-only local diagnostics found five Crashpad report sidecar files. Each has exactly:
```json
{"capture_kind":"crash","osarch":"x86_64","ptype":"browser"}
```

Their filesystem last-write times, converted to UTC, are approximately:
- 2026-10-18 10:37:09 UTC
- 2026-10-18 14:41:29 UTC
- 2026-10-18 15:19:55 UTC
- 2026-10-18 20:24:21 UTC
- 2026-10-18 20:45:03 UTC (new crash while unlocked)

For the earlier incident, the pre-crash desktop log ends at 2026-10-18T20:24:20.455Z, without a normal shutdown message in the inspected tail; a fresh process begins around 20:29:05 UTC.

For the new incident, the pre-crash log ends at 2026-10-18T20:45:02.299Z, the new Crashpad sidecar was written at approximately 20:45:03 UTC, and a fresh ChatGPT.exe process began at approximately 20:45:23 UTC. The final renderer entries have `rendererWindowFocused=true` and `rendererWindowVisible=true`. A scoped Kernel-Power 506/507 query shows no new Modern Standby interval between the 20:28:59 UTC resume and this crash.

No matching Codex/ChatGPT Application Error, Application Hang, or Windows Error Reporting event was found by the scoped Application log query.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The user initially noticed crashes after locking/unlocking Windows. On 2026-10-18 at approximately 20:45 UTC, they reported a further crash **without locking the computer**. No controlled reproduction is established.

The internal browser was in use before both recent crashes. In each case, the final log entries include browser tab teardown/close followed by an IAB routing failure (`Tab … is not part of browser session …`). This is a repeated temporal observation, not a proven crash trigger. Please investigate the tab close/detach lifecycle.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should remain running during normal unlocked use, including internal-browser tab operations, and recover normally after lock/unlock or suspend/resume.

### Additional information

Windows System logs show a Modern Standby interval surrounding the last observed crash:
- 2026-10-18 20:18:27 UTC: Kernel-Power event 506, entering Modern Standby, reason Idle Timeout.
- 2026-10-18 20:28:59 UTC: Kernel-Power event 507, exiting Modern Standby, reason Input Mouse.

This is correlation, not proof that Modern Standby caused the crash. The available sidecars do not include an exception code or stack trace, so no specific root cause is asserted.

The application was using its internal browser before the last crash; recent log entries include repeated `Frame with the given id was not found.` errors and a browser-tab routing error. These may be unrelated and should not be assumed to be the cause.

The initial diagnosis was read-only. After the first report, the Windows screen-off timeout was increased from 5 to 60 minutes on AC and battery; the sleep timeout remained at 120 minutes. The new crash occurred after that change. No Codex settings, user data, or installation files were modified. No matching Windows Resource-Exhaustion-Detector event was found in the scoped two-hour query; this alone does not rule out a process-local memory issue. Raw logs, conversation contents, account identifiers, and personal filesystem paths are omitted from this public report.

## Further local diagnosis and precautionary workaround (2026-10-18 UTC)

The final main-process logs were checked against **all five** observed Crashpad sidecars. Every run records an explicit CDP target-close lifecycle directly before exit:

| Target-close log time (UTC) | Crashpad sidecar write time, approximate (UTC) |
| --- | --- |
| 10:37:08.659 | 10:37:09 |
| 14:41:28.320 | 14:41:29 |
| 15:19:54.877 | 15:19:55 |
| 20:24:20.349 | 20:24:21 |
| 20:45:02.198 | 20:45:03 |

The corresponding local tool transcript establishes explicit awaited `tab.close()` calls at **20:24:20.203Z** and **20:45:02.073Z** for the two latest incidents. Tab variable names and business content are omitted. This strengthens the association with IAB tab closing; no native stack is available, so a specific native defect is still not proven.

Related existing reports: #53010, #43431, #42006, and #54493. The current installed `chrome.dll` file version is **155.0.8059.80**; this is different from the version described in #54493, so its exact fault offset cannot be assumed to apply here.

A data-preserving precaution was added to local agent instructions: reuse IAB tabs, avoid explicit tab-close cleanup, retain ongoing work with `markHandoff()`, and keep user-facing results with `markDeliverable()`. The turn-scoped retention mark must be renewed on later use because temporary tabs otherwise close at turn end. No app binaries, installed plugin code, browser cookies/storage, or chat databases were modified. A local online backup of chat databases was verified before applying the instruction change.

A short check opening a public documentation page, navigating, going back and reloading the **same retained IAB tab** completed without a new crash; the existing main process remained running and the Crashpad sidecar count remained five. The risky close operation was deliberately not repeated. This is **not evidence that the native bug is fixed**, and survival across later turns or long workloads remains to be verified. Please advise on a supported permanent fix that preserves existing chats and browser sessions.

items.body:
## Observed boundary
A user-authorized local validation run reached PowerShell and the fixed .NET Framework C# compiler. The compiler actually exited 0, and both output streams reached EOF. The following `System.Diagnostics.Process.Start()` for the newly compiled local test executable failed with the retained message `Windows Start failed: 拒绝访问`.

No test PID, child exit, test output, or case summary was produced: 0 of 70 planned native cases executed. The local runner used an absolute executable path, a matching working directory, `UseShellExecute=false`, redirected stdout/stderr, a hidden window, and three separate arguments. No shell command or URL was passed as the child executable.

The preserved occurrence was on October 18, 2026 UTC. A read-only package query on October 19 Asia/Shanghai reports OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0. That package measurement is not proof of which enforcement component handled the historical call. A separate product-owned GUI executable subsequently launched successfully; this does not establish a cause for the test executable's rejection.

## Diagnostic limitation
The retained wrapper preserved the message but not the original exception type, NativeErrorCode, HRESULT, enforcement rule or correlation ID. We therefore cannot attribute this to Defender, AppLocker, ACLs, an approval reviewer, or a particular Codex policy. This is also not the same observed boundary as the pre-shell `blocked by policy` event in #50979. No reliable fresh minimal reproduction has been established.

## Request
Please advise a supported, content-minimal way to identify the denial layer from existing records, and the minimum supported diagnostic/recovery procedure if a new run is required. Is there a supported distinction between an OS launch denial and a Codex execution restriction at this child-process boundary?

The refused executable has not been retried, renamed, moved, loaded in another host, or replaced by an alternative runner. No security, sandbox, permission, network, or installed-host settings were changed. Blocked cases remain unaccepted. We are requesting diagnostics that preserve enforcement, not a bypass.

Private project names, paths, chat/request identifiers, source, credentials, screenshots and raw logs are omitted.

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request
