items.body:
### Description

The Keyboard shortcuts settings page displays two substantially different layouts depending on the app’s Work/Codex mode, but both use the same **“Keyboard shortcuts”** heading.

I encountered both layouts during a session and initially thought shortcuts or customization features had disappeared. I may have changed modes, but I did not expect that to change the settings interface.

### What I observed

- A compact layout with toggle switches and sections such as **Composer**, showing fewer shortcuts.
- A full editor with shortcut search, multiple bindings per command, reset controls, and number-shortcut preferences.
- Shortcuts missing from the compact list continued to work.
- Settings search found **“Cycle reasoning effort”**, while the compact page showed **“Select effort”**, adding to the confusion.

The page later returned to the full editor.

### Investigation

Read-only inspection of the installed app bundle found both presentations in the same component. The default presentation depends on internal Work/Codex mode state.

This explains the different layouts. The investigation did not establish which action or state update caused the transition during my session.

### Suggested improvement

Use a heading that identifies the active presentation:

- **Keyboard shortcuts – ChatGPT**
- **Keyboard shortcuts – Codex**

The existing layouts and filtering can remain as they are. A clear heading would help users understand why the page changed and which shortcut settings they are viewing.

### Environment

- Windows
- Installed package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.3656.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`
- Observed: October 18, 2026

### Screenshots

Screenshot descriptions (images not attached):

1. Compact presentation showing Settings search for “cycle effort” and the Composer section.
2. Full shortcut editor after the presentation changed back.

items.title: Auto-compaction while IDE shows 51% context remaining: historical reasoning estimate differs from displayed usage

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: extension
labels.description: Issues related to the VS Code extension

labels.name: rate-limits
labels.description: Issues related to rate limits, quotas, and token usage reporting

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

items.body:
### Description

The Codex VS Code extension automatically compacted a conversation while its context indicator still showed approximately **51% remaining**. Logs show that the compaction guard uses an additional estimate of historical encrypted reasoning that the displayed API usage does not include.

This report concerns the disagreement between the visible indicator and the compaction budget. It does **not** assume that removing the additional estimate unconditionally is safe.

### Environment

- macOS arm64
- Codex VS Code extension: 26.1007.21434
- Original backend: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2
- Also reproduced the accounting difference with backend 0.163.0
- Model: gpt-6.1-sol
- Local custom model catalog overrides context_window and max_context_window to 1,050,000, with effective_context_window_percent=95
- Reported effective window: 997,500; automatic compaction threshold: 945,000

The window values above are local overrides, not a claim about the service's supported maximum.

### Exact accounting at the compaction trigger

| Component | Tokens |
|---|---:|
| API last_token_usage.total_tokens | 486,150 |
| Local estimate of encrypted reasoning before the latest user turn | 462,728 |
| Tool output after the latest model-generated item | 5,344 |
| Reconstructed total | **954,222** |
| Logged total_usage_tokens / auto_compact_scope_tokens | **954,222** |

The reconstruction matches exactly. The log reported:
- auto_compact_scope_limit=Some(945000)
- token_limit_reached=true
- full_context_window_limit=Some(997500)
- full_context_window_limit_reached=false

During the subsequent compaction request, API usage reported 490,422 input tokens and 3,964 output tokens.

### Relevant implementation

In [History::get_total_token_usage](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/history.rs#L937), when server_reasoning_included is false, get_non_last_reasoning_items_tokens() is added to the last API usage and the unreported trailing items.

Each historical encrypted reasoning item is estimated approximately as:
`ceil(max(0, floor(encoded_length * 3 / 4) - 650) / 4)`.

The HTTP/SSE and WebSocket implementations emit ServerReasoningIncluded(true) when the response/handshake contains x-reasoning-included. The observed totals establish that the fallback estimation branch was used; original response headers were not captured.

### Small reproduction of the accounting difference

An ephemeral conversation with backend 0.163.0, the same model and high reasoning effort was tested using HTTP/SSE, without working-chat history or MCP servers:

1. Ask for the smallest positive integer whose remainders modulo 17, 19 and 23 are 5, 7 and 11; request only the number and no tools.
2. Ask to verify the three remainders, again without tools.

Observed:
- Turn 1: API total=19,241; reasoning output=59; guard total=19,241.
- Turn 2: API total=23,672; reasoning output=40; guard total=23,896.

Changing from WebSocket to HTTP therefore did not remove the accounting difference. Updating to 0.163.0 did not resolve it either. Exact token counts will vary.

### Expected behavior / investigation requested

Please verify whether usage already includes historical reasoning for Responses Lite with reasoning.context=all_turns, and whether x-reasoning-included is propagated consistently across transports, reconnects and resumed sessions.

If historical reasoning still needs a local estimate, the IDE context indicator should expose a budget consistent with the compaction guard so compaction does not appear to occur with half the window unused. If the API already counts it, the client should avoid estimating it again.

No raw conversation contents, credentials or private project files are attached.

items.title: [macOS] Work sessions permanently stuck on "Awaiting approval" with no accessible composer or approval controls

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
Bug description
I am reporting a reproducible defect in ChatGPT Work that has rendered three separate Work sessions unusable.
Each session begins executing its assigned task but eventually enters a state displaying “Waiting for your answer” or “Awaiting approval.” At that point, the conversation becomes effectively read-only.
There is no accessible message composer, permissions control, approval button, or other mechanism for providing the requested authorization.
Consequently, I cannot approve the pending action, send another message, modify the instructions, or resume the session.
The problem has occurred in three separate Work conversations, including one deliberately simplified to test basic research functionality.
Environment
- Operating system: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Application: ChatGPT/Codex desktop application
- Subscription: ChatGPT Plus
- Browser tested: Google Chrome
- Project: Job search
- Date observed: October 18, 2026
- Application version: Not yet recorded
Steps to reproduce
1. Open the ChatGPT desktop application on macOS.
2. Open the existing Job Search project.
3. Initiate a Work session using ChatGPT's Work handoff functionality.
4. Assign a multistep task involving job research or application preparation.
5. Allow Work to begin executing the task.
6. Observe that Work eventually pauses with an “Awaiting approval” status.
7. Attempt to provide approval or continue the conversation.
Actual result: The session is stuck. No accessible composer, permissions control, or approval mechanism is available.
Expected result: When Work requires authorization, it should display an accessible approval control. The user should be able to approve or reject the action, modify instructions, or otherwise resume the conversation.
Affected sessions
The issue has occurred in three independent Work conversations:
1. Research remote $100K+ roles
Work was instructed to research remote positions matching my qualifications and compensation requirements.
The session entered an inaccessible approval state.
2. Launch job search workflow
Work was instructed to establish a broader job-search workflow involving research, resume tailoring, and application tracking.
This session also became stuck awaiting approval.
3. Find five qualifying remote roles
This was a deliberately simplified diagnostic test after the first two failures.
Work was instructed to identify five currently advertised remote positions, verify compensation and eligibility, and return direct posting links.
The instructions explicitly excluded creating files, logging into accounts, submitting applications, or requesting external authorization.
Nevertheless, Work began inspecting a job application at Mercury and subsequently entered the same inaccessible approval state.
This third failure demonstrates that the problem is not limited to complex workflows involving actual application submissions.
Additional issue: inconsistent conversation visibility
The three affected Work conversations are visible in the macOS application's Job Search project sidebar.
All three display green “Awaiting approval” indicators.
However, when opening the same project through Google Chrome, those conversations do not appear in the project's conversation list.
This prevents straightforward cross-platform troubleshooting.
OpenAI's AI support agent suggested that this discrepancy might relate to Local Work versus Work Cloud or local work synchronization. However, the original sessions were initiated through ChatGPT's Work handoff mechanism, and their local/cloud status has not been established.
The synchronization discrepancy may therefore be a separate issue.
Troubleshooting performed
The following troubleshooting steps have already been attempted:
1. Created three independent Work sessions.
2. Simplified the third task to eliminate application submissions, file creation, and account access.
3. Changed Cloud Browser website-access settings to permit automatic approval.
4. Attempted to interact with the stalled sessions through the macOS desktop application.
5. Opened ChatGPT in Google Chrome to investigate whether the missing approval controls were accessible there.
6. Consulted OpenAI's AI-assisted support agent.
None of these steps resolved the primary problem.
Information confirmed by OpenAI support
OpenAI's AI-assisted support agent confirmed the following:
- Work may legitimately pause for permissions or consequential-action confirmation.
- An accessible approval mechanism should be available when approval is required.
- A missing approval interface is not expected behavior.
- If the message composer and permissions control are inaccessible, there is no documented way to force approval or resume the affected turn.
- The support agent could not directly register a technical defect or escalate the issue to engineering.
- The agent directed me to the OpenAI Codex GitHub repository to report the malfunction.
Impact
This defect prevents completion of the assigned tasks and makes the affected Work conversations unusable.
The problem has been reproduced three times, resulting in several hours of lost time.
The inability to provide approvals is particularly serious because Work's execution model explicitly depends on user authorization for certain actions.
A session that requests approval but provides no means of granting it cannot function as intended.
Requested investigation
Please investigate:
1. Why Work sessions enter an approval state without displaying accessible approval controls or a message composer.
2. Whether this behavior is specific to the macOS desktop application, the Work handoff mechanism, or particular local/cloud execution modes.
3. Whether affected sessions can be recovered without restarting the entire workflow.
4. Why the affected conversations appear in the desktop project's sidebar but not in the corresponding browser project.
5. Whether there is a supported workaround for users experiencing this failure.
Please also consider implementing a recovery mechanism that allows users to reject a pending action, cancel the approval request, or resume a stalled session without losing its progress.
Attachments

items.title: cli: detect yarn and fallback pnpm in package manager detection

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

0.163.0 / latest main (`codex-cli`)

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### Which model were you using?

n/a (cli launcher)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

bash / xterm-256color

### Codex doctor report

not available

### What issue are you seeing?

in `codex-cli/bin/codex.js`, `detectPackageManager()` fails to detect `yarn` and falls back to `npm` for global `pnpm` installs executed outside directories containing `.modules.yaml`.

specifically:
1. if codex is installed globally via `yarn global add @openai/codex`, `yarn` is not recognized. the update prompt advises running `npm install -g @openai/codex@latest`.
2. if codex is installed via `pnpm add -g @openai/codex` but executed from an arbitrary directory (like `/tmp` or an empty workspace), `isPnpmOwnedCodexInstall()` returns `false` because there is no `.modules.yaml` in parent directories. lines 202-220 only check for `bun` before defaulting to `npm`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. install codex via yarn:
   ```bash
   yarn global add @openai/codex
   ```
2. inspect `detectPackageManager()` in `codex-cli/bin/codex.js` or trigger an update recommendation when an optional platform dependency is missing.
3. codex reports:
   ```text
   Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64. Reinstall Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
   ```
   instead of:
   ```text
   Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64. Reinstall Codex: yarn global add @openai/codex@latest
   ```

### What is the expected behavior?

`detectPackageManager()` should inspect `process.env.npm_config_user_agent` and `process.env.npm_execpath` for both `yarn` and `pnpm`:
- detect yarn and suggest `yarn global add @openai/codex@latest`
- detect pnpm from user agent when `.modules.yaml` is not in ancestor directories
- manage `CODEX_MANAGED_BY_YARN` environment variable

### Additional information

we have implemented and verified this fix in our fork with passing assertions:
- commit: https://github.com/phasehumans/codex/commit/b7f8f5d
- proposed diff:
```diff
diff --git a/codex-cli/bin/codex.js b/codex-cli/bin/codex.js
index 9346007..4d9cbbe 100755
--- a/codex-cli/bin/codex.js
+++ b/codex-cli/bin/codex.js
@@ -101,9 +101,11 @@ function findCodexExecutable() {
       ? "bun install -g @openai/codex@latest"
       : packageManager === "pnpm"
         ? "pnpm add -g @openai/codex@latest"
-        : packageManager === "vite-plus"
-          ? "vp install -g @openai/codex@latest"
-          : "npm install -g @openai/codex@latest";
+        : packageManager === "yarn"
+          ? "yarn global add @openai/codex@latest"
+          : packageManager === "vite-plus"
+            ? "vp install -g @openai/codex@latest"
+            : "npm install -g @openai/codex@latest";
   throw new Error(
     `Missing optional dependency ${platformPackage}. Reinstall Codex: ${updateCommand}`,
   );
@@ -216,6 +218,14 @@ function detectPackageManager() {
     return "bun";
   }
 
+  if (/\\bpnpm\\//.test(userAgent) || execPath.includes("pnpm")) {
+    return "pnpm";
+  }
+
+  if (/\\byarn\\//.test(userAgent) || execPath.includes("yarn")) {
+    return "yarn";
+  }
+
   return userAgent ? "npm" : null;
 }
 
@@ -225,9 +235,11 @@ const packageManagerEnvVar =
     ? "CODEX_MANAGED_BY_BUN"
     : packageManager === "pnpm"
       ? "CODEX_MANAGED_BY_PNPM"
-      : packageManager === "vite-plus"
-        ? "CODEX_MANAGED_BY_VITE_PLUS"
-        : "CODEX_MANAGED_BY_NPM";
+      : packageManager === "yarn"
+        ? "CODEX_MANAGED_BY_YARN"
+        : packageManager === "vite-plus"
+          ? "CODEX_MANAGED_BY_VITE_PLUS"
+          : "CODEX_MANAGED_BY_NPM";
 const env = {
   ...process.env,
   CODEX_MANAGED_PACKAGE_ROOT: codexPackageRoot,
@@ -235,6 +247,7 @@ const env = {
 delete env.CODEX_MANAGED_BY_NPM;
 delete env.CODEX_MANAGED_BY_BUN;
 delete env.CODEX_MANAGED_BY_PNPM;
+delete env.CODEX_MANAGED_BY_YARN;
 delete env.CODEX_MANAGED_BY_VITE_PLUS;
 env[packageManagerEnvVar] = "1";
```

items.title: Windows Codex Desktop: exec_command fails to resolve bundled pwsh.exe (0x80008085) despite valid file; explicit canonical D: shell still reports C: alias

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

On October 18, 2026, Codex Desktop on Windows x64 failed **before running any requested command** with:

```text
Failed to resolve full path of the current executable [%USERPROFILE%\.cache\codex-runtimes\codex-primary-runtime\dependencies\native\powershell\pwsh.exe]
```

Tool exit code: `-2147450747` / `0x80008085`.

The logical runtime path `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\codex-runtimes` is redirected to another volume, `D:\<redacted>\Codex-Runtimes`. Both the bundled `pwsh.exe` file and its containing directory exist. Read-only `stat` and `realpath` from the Codex-provided Node REPL resolve the alias to the D: target. Outside Codex, the same bundled PowerShell is Authenticode-signed by Microsoft and successfully runs `$PSVersionTable.PSVersion.ToString()` (7.6.5, exit code 0).

## Reproduction and evidence

1. In a local Codex Desktop workspace on D:, with its ordinary on-request approval and workspace-scoped sandbox, request `Get-Location` using the standard PowerShell shell. It fails before emitting command output.
2. Request one diagnostic tool invocation with the `shell` parameter explicitly set to the **canonical D: path** of `codex-primary-runtime\dependencies\native\powershell\pwsh.exe`, the existing workspace as `cwd`, `login=false`, and command `$PSVersionTable.PSVersion.ToString()`.
3. The recorded tool request includes the canonical D: executable, but its response again gives exit `-2147450747` and the error **naming the logical C: executable**. The command's execution and actual process image are unverified.

A session JSONL record confirms the canonical-path request on October 18 at approximately 21:16:26 UTC+03, with failure in the next second. The tool exposes combined output, not separate stdout/stderr.

## Sandbox and permissions context

- A sandbox log from October 18 records `MXC availability: true` and `Windows sandbox selection: mxc`. **Correlation of that selection to the exact canonical-path call has not independently been established.**
- Application configuration contains the enabled `prefer_mxc` feature.
- The submitted permission description for the test included `:root = read`, workspace-scoped writes, on-request/auto-reviewed approvals and disabled network access. No conflicting explicit deny rule was found in the inspected description. This is **not proof of effective native MXC access**.
- The selected UI approval mode remained stable; no transition to Custom was observed.
- No changes to ACLs, sandbox backend, junctions, cache, or system settings were made.

## Expected

The requested, existing, executable `pwsh.exe` should be resolved and launched within the effective sandbox policy, or the launcher should report the actual failing Windows operation and path, with a specific actionable diagnostic.

## Questions for maintainers

Could you trace:

- Requested `shell` argument vs internally selected bundled executable;
- Normalization/resolution of a redirected `%USERPROFILE%` runtime path to a D: target;
- Effective MXC policy materialization for both paths;
- The Windows API call that fails before process startup and its native status?

The underlying failing operation and root cause remain **unverified**. This report should not be interpreted as evidence that junctions or MXC permissions necessarily cause the failure.

## Related

- #53363: same error text and `0x80008085`, but a different reported permission-profile/UI scenario.
- #50915: MXC startup failures associated with BitLocker volume enumeration, **different error signature**.

No confidential files or raw logs are attached; personal paths are redacted.

items.body:
### App version

Microsoft Store/MSIX package `OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0` (x64), verified with Get-AppxPackage. The app window is titled ChatGPT and its manifest executable is `app/ChatGPT.exe`. Earlier supplied logs also show the affected package `26.1007.9446.0`. The About screen is inaccessible.

### Platform

Windows 10 22H2, build 19045, x64.
NVIDIA Quadro K620; driver 31.0.15.5255 (552.55), dated 2024-05-23.

### Problem

Launching ChatGPT opens the white startup window with the OpenAI logo, then the window closes without reaching a usable interface. After it disappears, `Get-Process -Name ChatGPT` returns no processes. This reproduces on repeated launches, including a launch from Start using Run as administrator.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch the installed ChatGPT desktop app from Start, or its registered AppUserModelID `OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0!App`.
2. Wait at the startup logo without submitting any prompt.
3. The window closes and the ChatGPT processes exit.

### Expected behavior

The app completes startup and stays open, displaying the sign-in screen or main interface.

### Troubleshooting completed

- Uninstalled the app, restarted Windows, downloaded and installed again: same behavior.
- Windows app reset: same behavior.
- Renamed `%APPDATA%\Codex` to a timestamped backup to test a fresh roaming profile: rename succeeded, same behavior. The backup was retained.
- Run as administrator from Start: same behavior.
- A diagnostic launch using IApplicationActivationManager with `--disable-gpu` produced no PowerShell error but the same startup/exit behavior. Whether the app honored this flag was NOT verified, so this does not conclusively exclude a GPU issue.
- Direct executable launch from a normal PowerShell session returned Access is denied; registered packaged activation succeeds. No WindowsApps permissions were changed.
- Windows Application/Reliability checks did not identify a corresponding ChatGPT crash report.

### Desktop log observations

Across the supplied attempts, the local app-server handshake succeeds, the main frame finishes loading, and the window reaches ready-to-show. Logs then stop without an explicit fatal error, process exit reason, or shutdown sequence.
